thread:
priya: FYI, after the keystore rotation at ~02:15 UTC we're seeing a big spike in GPU node provisioning fails. dozens of pods stuck in ContainerCreating, kubelet restarting sidecars with SIGKILL. anyone oncall?

alex: seeing same. logs show aws-kms decrypt failures: AccessDeniedException in eu-west-1. provisioning backoff.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: alert: cluster/gpu-provisioner high_retries on gpu-pool-eu-west-1 (started 02:20 UTC). link: https://alerts.redwood/1234

morgan: quick question — did security rotate the CMK or change key policy last night?

sasha: yes, we rotated the customer-managed key and tightened the key policy to remove some broad principals as part of audit fix. rollout was supposed to be staggered but looks like not all node-role variants were covered.

ian: digging into node logs now, paste relevant bit:

```
Feb 18 02:22:11 ip-10-0-5-12 kubelet[1234]: E0208 02:22:11.123456 1 kubelet.go:123] Failed to mount secret "keystore-config": failed to decrypt: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/node-role/i-01234 is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111111111111:key/old-key-id
Feb 18 02:22:11 ip-10-0-5-12 systemd[1]: keystore-agent.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
Feb 18 02:22:12 ip-10-0-5-12 kubelet[1234]: Back-off pulling secret, retrying
```

carla: also noticed an egress ACL change applied ~02:10 UTC that blocks outbound to kms.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com from subnet sg-prod-gpu-1. change set cs-9812. that would explain inability to reach KMS for some nodes.

morgan: so combined failure: key policy change removed decrypt permission for some node-role variants + egress ACL prevented network calls -> decryption fails locally -> agent retries and eventually OOM/SIGKILL -> provisioning backlog. makes sense.

priya: impact numbers: ~45 failed launches in last 30m, about 8 slow-successes, autoscaler moving to other AZs. rough cost exposure if this continues ~+$3k/hr in cross-AZ burst and reserved churn.

alex: proposed short-term mitigations: 1) relax egress ACL to allow kms endpoint for affected subnets, 2) temporarily re-grant kms:Decrypt to the old key policy for node-role, 3) restart keystore-agent ds to clear cached keys on nodes.

sasha: I can revert the ACL for a 10min window and re-add node-role to key policy as an emergency rollback. will coordinate with security approvers.

deploy-bot: changelog: reverted egress-acl cs-9812 -> success (02:36 UTC).

ian: after ACL revert we're seeing decrypt success lines again. running: `kubectl rollout restart ds/keystore-agent -n kube-system` now to clear cached state.

carla: rolling restart completed, nodes that were stuck started provisioning. observed a drop in backpressure and pod restarts.

morgan: followups: - add egress KMS endpoint reachability check to node preflight - add key-rotation staging plan that includes autoscaled pools and AMI variants - update runbook to include cross-check for ACL + key policy before rotating CMKs. opened PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4876

priya: thanks. leaving this thread as incident note. Oncall @alex please confirm capacity normal in 30m and mark incident if needed.

alex: will monitor dashboards. adding audit note: "Key rotation + egress ACL change caused transient GPU provisioning failures; mitigated by ACL rollback and daemonset restart." :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident-cluster: created incident INC-2026-02-18-gpu-provisioning (severity: low)

priya: closing the loop: security will coordinate a staged rotation with infra next run, and infra will add the preflight tests. thanks all.
